input.question: If our atmosphere was 78% Oxygen instead of nitrogen, would we be able to hold our breath longer?
input.ground_truth: If we hadn't been killed off by fires raging across continents every time there was a lightning storm, or exterminated by gigantic insects, sure. P.S. Insects are limited in size by their relatively inefficient pulmonary systems (and, possibly, their exoskeletons).

Explain the following question in a simple way as if you are explaining to a 5-year-old.

Question: If our atmosphere was 78% Oxygen instead of nitrogen, would we be able to hold our breath longer?

Answer:

response.prediction:
Let’s imagine you have a big jar of air to breathe. Right now, most of the air in the jar is made of something called “nitrogen,” and only a little bit is “oxygen,” which is what helps you stay alive.

But if the jar was mostly oxygen instead of nitrogen, the air would be very different. Oxygen is a special kind of air that your body needs every minute. If you breathe in too much oxygen and then hold your breath, your body gets confused. Too much oxygen can actually hurt you, even more than not having enough!

Also, your body uses up oxygen and makes a gas called “carbon dioxide.” If there’s a lot of oxygen, your body still makes carbon dioxide, and it builds up inside you when you hold your breath. That makes you want to breathe even more.

So, if the air was mostly oxygen, it would NOT be safer or easier to hold your breath. In fact, it might be more dangerous! Your body likes just the right mix of oxygen and other gases, like nitrogen, to stay healthy.
